text:
jana: Heads-up — seeing transient GPU node flapping in us-east1-b since 06:10. Small-batch generation p95 spiked ~50%. Preemptible nodes repeatedly entering TERMINATED. Anyone oncall?

ops-bot: node-autoscaler: detected 8 preemptible nodes flapping in pool 'spot-gpu-12g' (us-east1-b). Autoscale actions temporarily suspended for that pool.

ryan: I'm on it. Cloud console shows host-level maintenance events, many instances report 'host_preempted' as the termination reason.

tess: Traffic note — we had a short burst of long-context chat requests at 06:09 that increased queue depth. That could exacerbate eviction sensitivity, but primary signal looks provider-side.

siddharth: Mitigation proposal (short): 1) divert new requests from the spot pool to on-demand pool for affected routes, 2) increase on-demand nodes by +4 immediately, 3) temporarily reduce batch_size to keep tail latency low.

jana: I'll flip routing in ~15s and spin up on-demand. Can someone bump the on-demand autoscaler min so we don't cold-start too many?

mike: Bumping now — patching HPA minReplicas for on-demand deployment. Command:
```
kubectl patch hpa on-demand-gpu-hpa -p '{"spec":{"minReplicas":6}}'
```
Applied.

ryan: Thanks. Fallback is already handling ~30% of traffic but we still see retries leading to 503s from the frontend. Suggest set immediate fallback TTL to 0 to avoid retry storms.

tess: Also recommend removing preemptible scheduling for high-priority low-latency routes while we investigate. Which routes should be excluded? My vote: model-qa and chat-ll-low-latency.

jana: Route flip done for affected routes -> on-demand. Latency trending down to acceptable levels, monitoring.

ops-bot: metrics snapshot: p95 latency @06:15 = 220ms (was 480ms at peak). Preemptible pool size collapsed 12 -> 4. On-demand pool increased 2 -> 6.

siddharth: Cost delta FYI: extra on-demand capacity for ~30 min estimated ~$14.50. We'll absorb for SLO.

mike: Created follow-up task: ENGINFRA-1425 — "Improve autoscaler preference for stable nodes & add preemption health hook". Also added a quick alert to paging rules for repeated AZ flapping.

ryan: Ops action: request quota buffer for us-east1-b on-demand instances so repeated events don't push us into slow provisioning.

tess: Action items summary: (1) postmortem with timeline and root cause, (2) update runbook for AZ flapping/preemptible fallback, (3) scheduler policy change to prefer heterogeneous pools with weighted fallback, (4) tweak cost-alert thresholds for emergency spin-ups.

jana: I'll open the postmortem and assign owners. Thanks all — will update here with timeline and notes. :white_check_mark:

mike: tagging @siddharth for follow-up on the health hook and @ryan for quota ticket.

jana: closing loop for now — p95 stabilized. Keeping monitoring for 1 hour.
